reports.title: ADI Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Updates Full-Year Outlook

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: The Company is lowering its full-year 2026 outlook to reflect third-quarter performance and further weakness in Exclusive
Brands in October. The revised outlook assumes these demand and mix pressures persist through the remainder of the year.

($ in millions) | Nine Months Ended (1) | Q4 2026 | Full Year 2026
Net revenue | $3,798 | $1,112 - 1,132 | $4,910 - $4,930
Non-GAAP Adjusted Standalone EBITDA (Estimate) | $202 | $28 - $38 | $230 - $240
(1) Nine Months Ended 2026 represents results for the nine months ended October 3, 2026, as presented below.

desk.headline: Revenue up 9% to $1.31bn, beat; $659m goodwill write-down and full-year EBITDA outlook cut to $230–240m
results: Revenue rose 8.6% to $1.31bn, but average daily sales grew only 5%; two extra selling days and an easy comparison after last year's systems changeover did the rest.
Security, pro audio-visual, fire and data-communications sales grew, while residential audio-visual fell with the weak US housing market.
Gross margin fell to 20.9% from 22.6% on weaker mix and inventory charges; without tariff refunds and a spin-off inventory gain it was 20.0%.
A $659m goodwill write-down, triggered by residential weakness and the lower share price, produced a $655m net loss ($8.65 a share).
Cash was $208m at quarter-end, with a $500m revolving credit line undrawn; long-term debt stood at $980m.

guidance.summary: ADI cut its 2026 outlook for the first time as a standalone company: revenue to $4,910–4,930m from $4,950–5,000m and Adjusted Standalone EBITDA to $230–240m from $275–295m, implying a weak Q4.

points: Exclusive Brands daily sales fell 2% in Q3 and by high single digits in October; a mid-single-digit Q4 decline is now assumed, versus slight growth earlier.
Mix was the biggest drag on gross margin (about 140bp), followed by lapping last year's tariff benefit and freight and inventory charges; no quick recovery is expected.
For 2027, growth in third-party brands is expected to be largely offset by Exclusive Brands, and inflation plus the loss of about $24m of tariff refunds should absorb most of the $80m savings plan.
Further cost cuts are being prepared; net leverage is about 2.9 times against a 2.0 times target, and capital spending plans were reduced by $20m.
call.source: Earnings Whispers results and call summary (via Finviz), 12 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (13 Aug 2026)

watch: Exclusive Brands sales and whether the residential slowdown deepens.
Delivery of Q4 EBITDA within the $28–38m range and progress on extra cost cuts.
Gross margin trend and debt reduction towards the 2.0 times leverage target.
